title: Brown-Séquard and the Cord Syndromes: Which Side Is Weak, Which Side Is Numb?

hook.en: A half-cut spinal cord leaves one leg weak and the OTHER leg unable to feel pain. Damage the cord yourself in the lab, then read the body like an expert.

summaryEn: The cord holds three tracts: corticospinal (strength, SAME side), dorsal columns (position and vibration, SAME side), spinothalamic (pain and temperature, OPPOSITE side).

Brown-Séquard = same-side weakness and lost position sense, opposite-side lost pain and temperature; anterior = lost motor and pain with position kept; central = arms worse than legs; posterior = position lost, strength normal.
Protect the numb side from burns and pressure, respect spinal precautions, and treat a new or worsening cord picture, or autonomic dysreflexia, as an emergency.

next.title: Spasticity or Contracture? The Tardieu Catch Lab

title: Spasticity or Contracture? The Tardieu Catch Lab

hook.en: A stiff limb is not always "high tone". Stretch it slowly, then fast, and the muscle tells you whether the problem is the nervous system or the tissue itself. Do the test yourself.
hook.ur: Akri hui limb hamesha "high tone" nahi hoti. Pehle aahista, phir tez stretch karein, to muscle khud batata hai ke masla nervous system ka hai ya tissue ka. Test khud karke dekhein.

summaryEn: Spasticity is velocity-dependent: slow gives full range, fast gives an early catch. Rigidity resists equally at all speeds; contracture stops at the same angle at any speed.
Tardieu: R2 at the slowest speed is the muscle length, R1 at the fastest is the catch, X grades the reaction, and R2 − R1 is the neural part.

hook.en: Nerves slide and stretch when you move. Learn to test that movement, tell a nerve problem from a muscle problem, and treat with sliders or tensioners safely.

summaryEn: MET uses a gentle patient-made contraction followed by relaxation to improve range: light effort, a short hold, then take up the slack.

hook.en: Bones are not "put back in place". Learn the model of how hands-on treatment helps, and the words that calm patients instead of scaring them.

hook.en: Most painful shoulders are not torn. Learn the tests that separate cuff-related pain from a real tear, and the ones that point to instability or the AC joint.
hook.ur: Zyada tar dardnak shoulders phate hue nahi hote. Woh tests seekhein jo cuff ke dard ko asli tear se alag karte hain, aur woh jo instability ya AC joint ki taraf ishara karte hain.

next.title: Hip and Groin Pain — What to Test, What to Rule Out

hook.en: One in three older adults falls each year, and a fall can end independence. Exercise is the best-proven way to prevent falls. Learn to screen, to choose the right exercise and to build it into daily life.
hook.ur: Har saal teen mein se ek buzurg girta hai, aur ek girna khud mukhtari khatam kar sakta hai. Exercise girne se bachao ka sab se behtar sabit shuda tareeqa hai. Screen karna, sahi exercise chunna aur isay rozmarra zindagi mein shamil karna seekhein.

title: Differential Duels — Shoulder or Neck? Hip or Spine?

hook.en: The shoulder hurts, but the problem is in the neck. The groin hurts, but the problem is in the back. Experts win these duels with a few smart questions and tests, not with longer examinations. Learn the clues that tip the balance.
hook.ur: Kandha dukhta hai, lekin masla gardan mein hota hai. Groin dukhti hai, lekin masla kamar mein hota hai. Maahir yeh muqabilay lambay exam se nahi, chand samajhdar sawalon aur tests se jeette hain. Woh clues seekhein jo palra jhukate hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll run a short duel for shoulder versus neck and hip versus spine, use a cluster of findings instead of one test, and know when the answer is "both" or "neither".
goal.ur: End tak aap kandha versus gardan aur hip versus reedh ke liye chhota muqabla chalayenge, ek test ke bajaye findings ka cluster istemal karenge, aur jaanenge ke jawab kab "dono" ya "koi nahi" hota hai.

summaryEn: Pain can be referred, so test the joint above and below, and never diagnose from one test.
Use clusters (neck: Spurling, distraction, upper limb tension, rotation; hip: groin pain, internal rotation loss, scour) and change one thing to confirm.
The answer can be both, or neither; explain it clearly and refer when red flags or neurological change appear.

title: Rules Every Physio Should Know — Canadian C-Spine, NEXUS and Wells

hook.en: A patient walks in after a road crash with neck pain. Another has a swollen calf after surgery. Doctors use short clinical rules to decide who needs an X-ray or a clot test. You will use the same rules to decide who you can treat, and who must go.
hook.ur: Ek mareez sadak ke hadsay ke baad gardan ke dard ke saath aata hai. Doosre ki surgery ke baad pindli soojhi hui hai. Doctors chhote clinical rules se tay karte hain ke kis ko X-ray ya clot test chahiye. Aap wohi rules istemal karenge yeh tay karne ke liye ke kis ka ilaaj ho sakta hai aur kis ko bhejna hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll use the Canadian C-spine rule and NEXUS after neck trauma, apply the Wells score to a swollen calf, know the people each rule was built for, and say when a rule must NOT be used.
goal.ur: End tak aap gardan ki chot ke baad Canadian C-spine rule aur NEXUS istemal karenge, soojhi pindli par Wells score lagayenge, jaanenge ke har rule kin logon ke liye bana hai, aur kab rule istemal NAHI karna.

summaryEn: Decision rules sort patients into safe to carry on or needs the next step; they do not make the diagnosis.
After neck trauma, any high-risk factor, tingling, or inability to rotate 45 degrees means imaging before treatment; NEXUS needs all five criteria.
A swollen, tender calf after surgery or bed rest is a possible clot: stop, do not massage or exercise, and refer the same day.

next.title: Medicines That Change Your Rehab Plan — Six Patients, Six Surprises

title: Medicines That Change Your Rehab Plan — Six Patients, Six Surprises

hook.en: Behind every patient is a pill box that quietly changes how their body answers you. A heart rate that will not rise, a bruise that appears overnight, a tendon that gives way. Meet six patients who surprised their physios, and learn the one move that keeps each of them safe.
hook.ur: Har mareez ke peechay ek dawaiyon ka dibba hota hai jo khamoshi se tay karta hai ke un ka jism aap ko kya jawab dega. Dil ki raftar jo barhti nahi, raat bhar mein nikla neel, ek tendon jo toot gaya. Chhe mareezon se milein jinhon ne apne physios ko hairaan kiya, aur sikhein woh ek qadam jo har ek ko mehfooz rakhta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll recognise the main medicine families that change rehabilitation, know the surprise each one can cause, ask the four detective questions, and know when to adapt, when to report and when to call for help. You will never start, stop or change a medicine yourself.
goal.ur: End tak aap rehab badalne wali bari dawaiyon ke khandan pehchanenge, har ek ka hairaan karne wala asar jaanenge, chaar detective sawal poochhenge, aur jaanenge ke kab tabdeeli, kab report aur kab madad bulani hai. Aap kabhi khud koi dawai shuru, band ya tabdeel nahi karenge.

summaryEn: Medicines change the heart rate, bleeding, tendon strength, sugar and alertness, so ask about them before you load, press or push.
Use effort scales on beta-blockers, avoid deep pressure on blood thinners, and watch tendons after antibiotics or injections.
Never advise stopping a medicine; report your findings, and call for help for the danger signs.

title: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM)

hook.en: A sustained joint glide applied by the therapist while the patient performs the movement that normally hurts, aiming for an instant pain-free result.
hook.ur: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) mein therapist ek sustained accessory glide deta hai aur patient usi waqt apni active movement karta hai.
